en: Vimānavatthu:
The Chapter on the Pāricchattaka Tree in the Itthivimāna (The Female Vimānas)
2. The Story of the Mansion of Ucchudāyikā “Having illuminated the earth together with its devas,
you shine forth like the moon and the sun;”
In splendor, beauty, fame, and majesty,
you are like Brahmā among the thirty-three gods and their lord Indra.
I ask you, O wearer of the lotus garland:
Wearing a garland, with skin like gold,
adorned and clothed in the finest garments—
who are you, O auspicious deity, that pays homage to me?
What deed did you perform for yourself in the past,
when you were a human being in a previous birth—
was it the practice of giving, or was it the restraint of virtuous conduct?
“Having been reborn in a happy destination,
O renowned goddess, you have been questioned; tell us,
of what karma is this the fruit?”
“Now, venerable sir, you came to our house in this very village for alms;
then you gave us a piece of sugarcane.”
With a serene mind and incomparable joy,
my mother-in-law later questioned me:
"Where indeed, daughter-in-law, did you scatter the sugarcane?"
"It was neither discarded nor eaten by me;
I gave it myself to a peaceful bhikkhu.
This sovereignty is yours, and likewise mine."
Thus my mother-in-law reviled me;
taking a stool, she struck me.
Having passed away from there, I have become a deity.
That very same wholesome deed was performed by me,
and I myself experience the happiness resulting from that deed;
together with the devas, I enjoy myself.
I delighted in the five strands of sensual pleasure.
Yet that very wholesome deed was performed by me,
and I myself now experience the happiness resulting from that deed.
Guarded by the lords of gods and protected by the Thirty-three,
they are provided with the five strands of sensual pleasure.
Such is the abundant fruit of merit.
My offering of sugarcane has yielded a great karmic result;
together with the devas,
I enjoy myself and delight in the five strands of sensual pleasure.
Such is the abundant fruit of merit from this gift of sugarcane to me, which possesses great radiance;
it is guarded by the Lord of Devas and protected by the gods of the Thirty-three.
Just as [Indra] with a thousand eyes in the Nandana grove,
I approached you, O Bhante, the compassionate and wise one,
paid homage, and asked after your well-being.
Then, with a mind full of faith and incomparable joy, she gave him a piece of sugarcane.
Thus ends the second Vimāna, the Ucchudāyikā-vimāna.
